Pope Leo XIV appears on the central balcony of St. Peter's Basilica at the Vatican to bless the crowd below on May 11, 2025.

**Updated May 18, 2025 at 5:52 AM CDT**

VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo XIV, history's first American pope, vowed Sunday to work for unity so that the Catholic Church becomes a sign of peace in the world, offering a message of communion during an inaugural Mass in St. Peter's Square before an estimated 150,000 pilgrims, presidents, patriarchs and princes.

Leo officially opened his pontificate by taking his first popemobile tour through the piazza, a rite of passage that has become synonymous with the papacy's global reach and mediatic draw. The 69-year-old Augustinian missionary smiled and waved from the back of the truck, but didn't appear to stop to kiss babies and the crowd.

During the Mass, Leo appeared to choke up when the two potent symbols of the papacy were placed on him — the pallium woolen stole over his shoulders and the fisherman's ring on his finger — as if the weight of responsibility of leading the 1.4-billion strong church had just sunk in.

He turned his hand to look at the ring and seal and then clasped his hands in front of him in prayer.

U.S. Vice President JD Vance, one of the last foreign officials to see Pope Francis before he died, led the U.S. delegation honoring the Chicago-born Leo after paying his respects at the Argentine pope's tomb upon arriving in Rome late Saturday.

The theme of Leo's papacy
-------------------------

In his homily, Leo said he wanted to be a servant to the faithful through the two dimensions of the papacy, love and unity, so that the church could be a force for peace in the world.

"I would like that our first great desire be for a united church, a sign of unity and communion, which becomes a leaven for a reconciled world," he said. "In this our time, we still see too much discord, too many wounds caused by hatred, violence, prejudice, the fear of difference, and an economic paradigm that exploits the Earth's resources and marginalises the poorest."

His call for unity was significant, given the polarization in the Catholic Church in the United States and beyond.

Francis' radical 12-year pontificate, which emphasized care for the poor and marginalized and disdain for the capitalist economic system, often alienated conservatives and traditionalists. Leo's May 8 election, after a remarkably quick 24-hour conclave, has appeared at the outset to have pleased conservative Catholics who seem to appreciate his more disciplined, traditional style and Augustinian background, emphasizing core truths of Catholic doctrine.

"Let us build a church founded on God's love, a sign of unity, a missionary church that opens its arms to the world, proclaims the word, allows itself to be made restless by history, and becomes a leaven of harmony for humanity," Leo said, referencing some of the themes of Francis' pontificate as well.

At the end of the Mass, Leo expressed hope for negotiations to bring a "just and lasting peace" in Ukraine and offered prayers for the people of Gaza — children, families and elderly who are "reduced to hunger," he said. Leo made no mention of hostages taken by Hamas from southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, as Francis usually did when praying for Gaza.

AP

Pope Leo XIV holds Mass during the formal inauguration of his pontificate in St. Peter's Square attended by heads of state, royalty and ordinary faithful, Sunday, May 18, 2025.

Tight security and protocol
---------------------------

Strict diplomatic protocol dictated the seating arrangements at the inaugural Mass, with both the United States and Peru getting front-row seats thanks to Leo's dual citizenship. Vance, a Catholic convert who tangled with Francis over the Trump administration's mass migrant deportation plans, was joined by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who arrived in Rome ahead of time to try to advance Russia-Ukraine peace talks.

Peruvian President Dina Boluarte is one of around a dozen heads of state attending, as well as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Russia was represented by the culture minister, Olga Liubimova.

After the Mass, Leo greeted the delegations one-by-one in the basilica and had proper audiences scheduled Sunday with Zelenskyy and Boluarte.

Diplomatic protocol also dictated the dress code: While most wore black, the handful of Catholic queens and princesses — Charlene of Monaco and Letizia of Spain among others — wore white in a special privilege allowed them. Three dozen of the world's other Christian churches sent their own delegations, the Jewish community had a 13-member delegation, half of them rabbis. Other representatives headed Buddhist, Muslim, Zoroastrian, Hindu, Sikh and Jain delegations.

Security was tight, as it was for Francis' funeral on April 26, which drew an estimated 250,000 people. The Vatican said 150,000 were on hand Sunday in the piazza and surrounding streets, parks and piazzas, where giant television screens and portable toilets were set up.

Americans are rejoicing
-----------------------

U.S. seminarian Ethan Menning, 21, from Omaha, Nebraska, wrapped himself in an American flag, purchased at a truck stop in Iowa, to celebrate.

"Rome always felt like home for a Catholic, but now coming here and seeing one of our own on the throne of Peter ... it almost makes Jesus himself more accessible," he said.

Kalen Hill, a pilgrim from the U.S., got to St. Peter's soon after the gates opened at dawn Sunday morning and said he never expected an American would lead the church.

"I would say all the Americans are emotional about it," he said. "It is really powerful for American Catholics who sometimes feel separated from the world church to be brought in and included in this community through Pope Leo."

Signs of Leo's priorities
-------------------------

The two symbols of the papacy handed to Leo were the pallium, and the fisherman's ring. The pallium, draped across his shoulders, symbolizes the pastor carrying his flock as the pope carries the faithful. The ring, which becomes Leo's official seal, harks back to Jesus' call to the apostle Peter to cast his fishing nets.

The other symbolically important moment of the Mass was the representational rite of obedience to Leo: Whereas in the past all cardinals would vow obedience to the new pope, more recent papal installations involve representatives of cardinals, bishops, priests, deacons, nuns, married couples and young people participating in the rite.

Gregory and Susan Hudak, who lived for 40 years in the Chicago area, found themselves in Rome after booking a trip in February, with just a faint hope of perhaps glimpsing the pope. Seeing the popemobile pass by in front of them, with the Chicago-born Leo on board, was even better than watching Michael Jordan play, said Gary Hudak, a former altar boy wearing a Chicago Bears hat.

"Originally, the only hope I had coming here was to see the inside of the Sistine Chapel," he said. "Seeing the pope was not scheduled, it was a long shot hope. And this was a treasure, simple as that."

'God loves Peru': Country celebrates new Pope as one of their own
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Ione Wells,South America Correspondent, Peruand

Guillermo D Olmo & Helen Sullivan,BBC News Mundo and BBC News

'Gift from heaven': Peruvians react to the election of Pope Leo XIV

Halfway through Leo XIV's first speech as pope, which he delivered in Italian, he stopped and asked if he might say a few words in Spanish.

Smiling, he continued: "A greeting to all and in particular to my dear Diocese of Chiclayo, in Peru."

The first American pope is a citizen of Peru and has spent much of his life there, travelling between the two countries for decades until 2014, when Pope Francis appointed him bishop of the Chiclayo Diocese in the country's north.

On Thursday, Peruvians rejoiced at the appointment of one of their own to the highest position in the Catholic Church.

Standing near Lima's cathedral shortly after bells rang out in celebration of the appointment, elementary school teacher Isabel Panez said: "For us Peruvians, it is a source of pride that this is a pope who represents our country."

Prevost would often say that he had "come from Chicago to Chiclayo – the only difference is a few letters," Diana Celis, who attended several Masses officiated by the then Bishop Robert Prevost, told the Associated Press news agency.

He reportedly referred to Peru, where around three quarters of people are Catholic, as "mi segunda patria" – my second homeland.

Peru's president, Dina Boluarte, described Pope Leo as Peruvian "by choice and conviction".

"The pope is Peruvian; God loves Peru," she said.

*   [Follow our live updates](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cn4we7prv4rt)
*   [Pope Leo XIV marks new beginning for Catholic Church](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckgrwy5pyyjo)
*   [Continuity the key for Pope seen as unifier in the Church](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c4g2epnpr3ko)
*   [Who is the new pope, Robert Prevost?](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c0ln80lzk7ko)

Born in Chicago in 1955, he is the son of Louis Marius Prevost, of French and Italian descent, and Mildred Martinez, of Spanish descent.

After completing studies in theology in Chicago and in canon law in Rome, the Catholic Church sent him to Peru for the first time.

He arrived at the Augustinian mission in Chulucanas, in the Peruvian department of Piura, in 1985, aged 30, and the following year, joined the mission in Trujillo. For almost three decades, he worked between the US and Peru.

Then, in 2014, Pope Francis appointed Prevost bishop of Chiclayo, a position he assumed the following year, after becoming a Peruvian citizen.

Jose Luis Perez Guadalupe, who was the minister responsible for signing Prevost's naturalisation, told BBC Mundo that he was "a very attentive and very thoughtful man, who listened more than he spoke."

These were his first encounters with a country that would come to shape his life.

![Image 1](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20251210-151139-37baf2dfdd-web-2.36.1-1/grey-placeholder.png)![Image 2: Reuters A group of mainly women cheer with their hands in the air and hold a banner of Pope Louis XIV](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/8092/live/1993e140-2c90-11f0-8683-9b1503cf649e.jpg.webp)Reuters

People celebrate at the Cathedral of Saint Mary in Chiclayo, Peru with a banner saying Pople XIV has a Chiclayo heart.

Janinna Sesa, who met Prevost while she worked for the church's Caritas nonprofit, told the Associated Press during torrential rains in 2022 he waded through mud to help people in Chiclayo and nearby villages.

He also delivered food and blankets to remote Andean villages, driving a white pickup truck and sleeping on a thin mattress on the floor. There, Sesa said, Prevost ate whatever was offered to him, including the peasant diet consisting of potatoes, cheese and sweet corn.

But, if the opportunity came up, he would enjoy carne asada – one of his favorite dishes – accompanied by a glass of Coca-Cola.

He also had an interest in cars. "He has no problem fixing a broken-down truck until it runs," Sesa said.

Prevost was the driving force for the purchase of two oxygen-production plants during the coronavirus pandemic, which killed more than 217,000 people across Peru.

"He worked so hard to find help, that there was not only enough for one plant, but for two oxygen plants," Sesa said.

Edinson Farfán, the Peruvian Bishop of Chiclayo since 2024, said Pope Leo would continue Pope Francis's legacy of working with the poor and advocating for "a Church with open doors". He was "very close to Pope Francis", he said.

"He was undoubtedly deeply influenced by this particular Church of Chiclayo. Chiclayo is a city that greatly values the simple faith of its people. He has a special affection for the diocese."

"It's his beloved diocese, it's his life. He learned here everything he can share and will share with the entire world."

![Image 3](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20251210-151139-37baf2dfdd-web-2.36.1-1/grey-placeholder.png)![Image 4: Reuters A group of people stand smiling in front of the cathedral in Chicalyo, Peru. One holds a picture of Pope Leo XIV.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/a4a9/live/37a1ee30-2c8f-11f0-8683-9b1503cf649e.jpg.webp)Reuters

A woman holds an image of Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost in front of the Cathedral of Saint Mary in Chiclayo, Peru, after he was elected the new Pope, 8 May 2025

But not all in the country are proud of his record.

Serious accusations have been made about his handling of sexual abuse cases during his time as Bishop of Chiclayo.

In 2023, three Peruvian women went public with claims that as bishop he failed to investigate their reports of having been abused as teenagers by two priests in Chiclayo, dating back to 2007. They said that when they raised their allegations with the diocese in 2022, no proper inquiry was opened.

Church officials in Chiclayo said that action was taken and the accused priests were put on precautionary suspension, and that the case was referred to the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, which handles serious abuse cases.

The diocese said it was Rome's decision to shelve the case without a full canonical trial and that it conducted a preliminary investigation.

These allegations about his leadership are one of the challenges he will face as he now heads the Church worldwide.

![Image 5](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20251210-151139-37baf2dfdd-web-2.36.1-1/grey-placeholder.png)![Image 6: EPA This picture is taken from the back of the church, and shows people sitting in wooden pews in mass, facing a painting of Jesus Christ on the cross. ](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/3636/live/16c97ad0-2c89-11f0-adf6-eb691186d878.jpg.webp)EPA

A mass at Las Nazarenas Church, in Lima, Peru, 8 May 2025.

Perez Guadalupe said that while Prevost primarily remained focused on church matters in Peru, he was "very attentive to the reality" of the country.

In 2023, when violent anti-government protests following the ousting of then-president Pedro Castillo left 49 dead, Prevost told Peruvian media he felt "much sorrow and much pain".

That year, Pope Francis called Prevost to Rome to serve as the prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops, the powerful head of the office that vets bishop nominations from around the world and one of the most important jobs in the Catholic Church. He was also appointed president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America.

Prevost said that he had asked Pope Francis to allow him to remain in Peru longer.

As he heard Prevost was the new pope, Thomas Nicolini, a Peruvian who studies economics in Rome, went to St Peter's Square.

He told the AP that Chiclayo is, "A beautiful area, but one of the regions that needs lots of hope."

"So, now I'm expecting that the new pope helps as many people as possible, and tries to reignite, let's say, the faith young people have lost."

![Image 3](https://catholicweekly.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251209T1145-VATICAN-ANNUARIO-YEARBOOK-DIGITAL-1809278.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV tries a new digital platform of the Vatican’s yearbook, known as the Annuario Pontificio, at the Vatican Dec. 6, 2025. (CNS photo/screengrab courtesy Vatican Secretary of State)

The Vatican’s fat red yearbook, known as the Annuario Pontificio, will now be available and updated regularly on an app and online.

The digital platform “will guarantee reliable and immediate access to certified content, promoting an accurate and documented account of the life of the church,” the Vatican Secretariat of State said in a press release 9 December.

The pontifical yearbook lists: all Vatican offices and staff; the world’s dioceses and mission territories; bishops, cardinals and international religious orders of men and women; papal diplomats and ambassadors to the Vatican; historical notes, such as a list of the popes and their years in office, and more.

\- Advertisement -

Archbishop Edgar Peña Parra, substitute for general affairs in the secretariat, and others met with Pope Leo XIV 6 December to present the initiative and to let him try searching the platform on a tablet.

“Thank you for this work, which will be of great use to so many people who work serving the church,” the pope told those present. “I encourage you to continue in this spirit of service, so that what is established with care and attention may become an even greater help over time.”

![Image 4](https://catholicweekly.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251209T1145-VATICAN-ANNUARIO-YEARBOOK-DIGITAL-1809279.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV tries a new digital platform of the Vatican’s yearbook, known as the Annuario Pontificio, at the Vatican Dec. 6, 2025. (CNS photo/screengrab courtesy Vatican Secretary of State)

Archbishop Parra said, “The digitisation of the Pontifical Yearbook represents a significant step in the renewal of the Holy See’s tools of service. At a time when communication is increasingly rapid and global, offering immediate and reliable access to information on the life of the church – with certified data – means putting technology at the service of the church’s mission.”

The thick, hardcover yearbook typically numbers more than 2,500 pages and is available only in Italian. Printed once a year, the Vatican used to send out changes and updates once or twice a month via email and post them online. Officials from the Secretariat of State are responsible for updating the volume.

Now, as a digital resource, information will be revised and updated more often, the secretariat’s press release said.

After creating an account online and paying the annual subscription fee ($79), the online version is available at [annuariopontificio.catholic](https://www.annuariopontificio.catholic/welcome) or on an app optimised for smartphones and tablets.

After the initial rollout, the platform will add expanded capabilities, such as other languages and past data for archival purposes.

The hardcopy volume will still be published, the secretariat said, because of the historical value of such documentation.

                        The
                          Popes

                          The title of 'pope' has been used since the 5th century
                          to designate the head of the Roman Catholic Church,
                          regarded as the successor of St Peter. In the early
                          centuries of Christianity, the pope was simply the Bishop
                          of Rome and did not possess formal authority over other
                          bishops. However, over time, the pope came to be recognised
                          as the supreme authority within the Church, and the
                          scope of his powers gradually expanded. The Vatican's
                          Annuario Pontificio lists the pope’s
                          full titles, which include: Bishop of Rome, Vicar of
                          Jesus Christ, Successor of the Prince of the Apostles,
                          Supreme Pontiff of the Universal Church, Primate of
                          Italy, Metropolitan Archbishop of the Province of Rome,
                          Sovereign of the State of Vatican City, and Servant
                          of the Servants of God. The title 'Patriarch of the
                          West' was historically included, but it was officially
                          removed in 2006.

| [![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Pope_Leo_XIV_3_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_3_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_3_/(cropped/).jpg) |

 |

A [conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave "Conclave") was held on 7 and 8 May 2025 to elect a new [pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope "Pope") to succeed [Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis "Pope Francis"), who had died on 21 April 2025. Of the 135 eligible [cardinal electors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_electors_in_the_2025_conclave "Cardinal electors in the 2025 conclave"), all but two attended. On the fourth ballot, the conclave elected Cardinal [Robert Francis Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Francis_Prevost "Robert Francis Prevost"), the prefect of the [Dicastery for Bishops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Bishops "Dicastery for Bishops") and president of the [Pontifical Commission for Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Latin_America "Pontifical Commission for Latin America"). After accepting his election, he [took the name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") _Leo XIV_.

Papal election process
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Papal election process")\]

The papal election process proper began sixteen days after the 21 April 2025 [death of Pope Francis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_funeral_of_Pope_Francis "Death and funeral of Pope Francis"). As in the [2013 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_conclave "2013 conclave"), the [dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_of_the_College_of_Cardinals "Dean of the College of Cardinals") and vice-dean of the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") were both over 80 and ineligible to participate. In 2025, these were [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re") and [Leonardo Sandri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonardo_Sandri "Leonardo Sandri"), respectively. The most senior elector under 80, [Pietro Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin"), who was also Cardinal Secretary of State, presided over the 2025 conclave.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-1)

### Timing and procedures

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Timing and procedures")\]

According to [John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Paul_II "John Paul II")'s 1996 apostolic constitution _[Universi Dominici gregis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universi_Dominici_gregis "Universi Dominici gregis")_, as amended by [Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict XVI")'s 2013 apostolic letter _[Normas nonnullas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normas_nonnullas "Normas nonnullas")_,[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Bonanata_2025-2)[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Caputo_2025-3) the [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") had at least 15 days after the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") became vacant to convene. The cardinals had the discretion to start the conclave earlier or up to 20 days after the pope's [cathedra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedra "Cathedra") became vacant.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Bonanata_2025-2) On 28 April 2025, two days after Francis's funeral,[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-4) the fifth general congregation of the cardinals set the conclave to begin on 7 May 2025.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-6)

Cardinals aged 80 years or older on the day before the papacy fell vacant were ineligible to participate. At the time of Francis' death, there were 252 cardinals, of whom 135 were under 80 and thus were not precluded from participation and voting in the conclave.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7) Of these potential electors, 108 (80%) had been elevated to the College of Cardinals by Francis;[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-9) the cardinal electors were also global and more diverse than in any prior conclave — they came from more than 70 countries and in many cases were the first cardinal ever appointed from their country.[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-10)

Since the 1975 promulgation of _[Romano Pontifici eligendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano_Pontifici_eligendo "Romano Pontifici eligendo")_ by [Pope Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI "Pope Paul VI") and the 1996 apostolic constitution _[Universi Dominici gregis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universi_Dominici_gregis "Universi Dominici gregis")_ by [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II"), the maximum number of cardinal electors had been 'set' at 120.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Hodge-2025-11)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-12) At 133, the 2025 conclave was the largest ever,[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-13) and the first conclave where this purported limit was exceeded on the day the papacy became vacant.[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-120+-15)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Campisi_&_Gussie_2025-14) Any cardinal under the age of 80 not having renounced or lost his voting rights has the right to vote in a conclave under [Catholic canon law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_canon_law "Catholic canon law"). A pope appointing more than 120 eligible cardinal electors effectively renders the 1975 limit inapplicable,[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16) as popes John Paul II, Benedict XVI, and Francis all did;[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Campisi_&_Gussie_2025-14) although in the cases of John Paul II and Benedict XVI, the 120 limit at the conclave was not surpassed.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Hodge-2025-11)

On 30 April 2025, the general congregation of cardinals confirmed that all cardinal electors present for the conclave beginning on 7 May could vote.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-17) Ineligible cardinals could nevertheless attend the general congregations and participate in discussions preceding the conclave.[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-18) Although the conclave cardinals have the authority to elect any Catholic male who has been [baptized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptized "Baptized"),[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Caputo_2025-3) the last time a non-cardinal was elected was in the [1378 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1378_conclave "1378 conclave").[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-19)[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-20)

After saying he would try to participate in the conclave,[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-21) Cardinal [Giovanni Angelo Becciu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Angelo_Becciu "Giovanni Angelo Becciu"), who had "renounced his rights as a cardinal" in 2020 due to his involvement in a financial scandal,[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Pinto-2025-22) stated that he would abide by Francis's wish that he refrain from participating.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-23) Health problems prevented cardinals [Antonio Cañizares Llovera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Ca%C3%B1izares_Llovera "Antonio Cañizares Llovera") of Spain and [John Njue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Njue "John Njue") of Kenya from participating in the conclave,[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-24) reducing the number of potential electors to 133; accordingly, the two-thirds supermajority required to elect the new pope was determined at 89 votes. This was the largest number of cardinal electors ever to participate and vote in a conclave.[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-25)

Francis's hospitalization in February and March 2025 fueled speculation about an impending conclave.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-26) Due to the major international expansion of the membership of the College of Cardinals under Francis to 252, with over 140 non-European [cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_/(Catholic_Church/) "Cardinal (Catholic Church)") appointed during his pontificate, some observers had suggested a non-European pope was likely.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7)[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16) The 2025 conclave was initially planned to have 135 electors from 71 countries; the 2013 and 2005 conclaves had had 115 electors from 48 and 52 countries respectively. Some of the participating cardinals did not speak Italian, the [working language of the Roman Curia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_language_of_the_Roman_Curia "Working language of the Roman Curia").[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Dom%C3%ADnguez-2025-27)

Following the Italian saying "[fat pope, thin pope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat_pope,_thin_pope "Fat pope, thin pope")", some commentators predicted that Francis's successor would be more conservative.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Jeyaretnam-2025-16)[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-28) There were also concerns of interference, which had been prohibited in 1996 by John Paul II,[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-29) and a potential hostile takeover by [ultraconservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraconservative "Ultraconservative") politicians and Catholics.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-31) As of the third and fourth general congregations, there was reportedly a desire among the cardinals for a ten-year pope, someone in his late seventies with experience in the [Roman Curia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Curia "Roman Curia") who would be more focused on internal affairs.[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-32)

Some commentators posited a younger pope as more likely;[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-33) others felt that cardinals like [Pierbattista Pizzaballa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierbattista_Pizzaballa "Pierbattista Pizzaballa") and [Robert Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Prevost "Robert Prevost") were too young.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-BBC-2025-7)[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-34)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-35) Many cardinals expressed hope for a short conclave, as in 2005 and 2013.[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-36) Given the complexities and heterogeneity of this conclave,[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-37) compared to the two-day one that elected Francis in 2013,[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38) Cardinal [Rainer Woelki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainer_Woelki "Rainer Woelki") expected the 2025 conclave to take longer;[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38) the Cardinals [Louis Raphaël I Sako](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Rapha%C3%ABl_I_Sako "Louis Raphaël I Sako") and [Gregorio Rosa Chávez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorio_Rosa_Ch%C3%A1vez "Gregorio Rosa Chávez") anticipated a short conclave of two or three days,[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-39)[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-40) with the latter remarking "maximum three days".[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-41)[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-42)

[Vaticanologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaticanologist "Vaticanologist") consider (by a variety of criteria) some cardinals to be more likely to become pope than others – these are the _[papabili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papabili "Papabili")_ (the plural for _papabile_), Italian for "pope-able".[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-43) In practice, however, conclaves have not always chosen one of the _papabili_. Prior to his election in the [October 1978 conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_1978_conclave "October 1978 conclave"), [John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Paul_II "John Paul II") was not considered to be in the running.[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-44) This is reflected in the saying "He who enters the conclave as pope, leaves it as a cardinal,"[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-45) although the frontrunner is often elected pope, as was the case in [1939](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1939_conclave "1939 conclave") ([Pius XII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pius_XII "Pius XII")), [1963](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1963_conclave "1963 conclave") ([Paul VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI "Paul VI")), and [2005](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_conclave "2005 conclave") ([Benedict XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benedict_XVI "Benedict Before the announcement of the conclave itself, prediction markets were using market mechanisms to calculate who might be in the running and their putative rankings.[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-61)[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-62)[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-63) Upon Francis's death, the top five contenders were Tagle, Parolin, Zuppi, Ambongo, and Erdő, all of whom had been cited by Vatican journalists and analysts as _papabili_.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-64) On the day of Prevost's election, the leading candidates on [Polymarket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymarket "Polymarket") were Parolin at 37%, Tagle at 26%, Pizzaballa at 10%, Erdő at 8%, Turkson at 7%, Sarah at 4%, and Zuppi at 3%. Parolin's odds to be named as the new pope jumped to nearly 70% after the white smoke was revealed, with many suspecting that the relatively short four-round conclave indicated a consensus candidate had been chosen.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-65)

Fantapapa ([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") for 'Fantasy Pope') was a [fantasy league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_league "Fantasy league") based in Italy for betting nominal sums on [papal conclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave "Conclave"). Established by anti-gambling advocates Pietro Pace and Mauro Vanetti specifically for the 2025 conclave,[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-66) the sole payout was "eternal glory". By 5 May 2025, it had 75,000 players in Italy, where no licensed platform offers gambling on conclaves.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-67) Fantapapa players chose from and ranked eleven cardinals; other aspects of the conclave, such as the papal name, language, number of rounds, and the day on which white smoke appears, were also available to bet on. Players gained points in accordance to their team members being "mentioned prominently" in domestic and international media coverage. The fantasy league was open to punters internationally and also offered mini-lessons in the Italian language.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-68)

### Logistical preparations

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Logistical preparations")\]

[![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg/250px-Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Domus_Sanctae_Marthae.jpg)

Cardinals participating in the conclave stayed at [Domus Sanctae Marthae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae "Domus Sanctae Marthae").

Following the death of Pope Francis, preparations began at Domus Sanctae Marthae for housing the cardinal electors. These included setting up barriers or opaque film at the windows to prevent outside contact and the construction of spaces for the celebration of the [Sacrament of Penance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrament_of_Penance "Sacrament of Penance"), private prayer, and meals.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Il_Mattino-2025-69)[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70) [Signal jammers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signal_jammers "Signal jammers") were used to isolate the electors from [Bluetooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth "Bluetooth"), [Wi-Fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wi-Fi "Wi-Fi"), and [mobile networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_network "Mobile network").[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70)[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-71)[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) Because the building has only 129 bedrooms, it was necessary to provide accommodations for the 133 electors and support personnel,[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-73)[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-74)[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-75) who stayed at Santa Marta Vecchia, next door to the main dormitory.[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-76)[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_Review-2025-77)[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-78)

In the Sistine Chapel, preparations included the addition of tables and chairs in the manner of [choir stalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choir_stalls "Choir stalls") and the covering of windows; the ballot-burning stove and the chimney, which together serve to signal the results to the outside world, were installed,[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-79)[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-The_Washington_Post-2025a-80) as was a temporary wooden floor which served to protect the marble inlay, provide a more level surface, and hide electronic signal jammers.[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-The_Washington_Post-2025a-80)[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-NPR-81) Both the Domus Sanctae Marthae and the Sistine Chapel were thoroughly inspected in advance of the conclave for any unauthorized devices.[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70) On 2 May, [Vatican firefighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Firefighters_of_the_Vatican_City_State "Corps of Firefighters of the Vatican City State") installed the chimney for the Sistine Chapel.[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-82)

The [Vatican Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Gendarmerie "Vatican Gendarmerie"), under the leadership of [Gianluca Gauzzi Broccoletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluca_Gauzzi_Broccoletti "Gianluca Gauzzi Broccoletti"), faced many [counter-espionage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter-espionage "Counter-espionage") challenges in protecting conclave integrity.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Dom%C3%ADnguez-2025-27)[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Garay-2025-70)[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) The [Corps of Gendarmerie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Gendarmerie_of_Vatican_City "Corps of Gendarmerie of Vatican City") used the 650 [security cameras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Security_cameras "Security cameras") in the Vatican, [encrypted messaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encrypted_messaging "Encrypted messaging"), and [endpoint detection and response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endpoint_detection_and_response "Endpoint detection and response") to secure the conclave.[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Cybernews-2025-72) Meals for the 2025 conclave featured simple dishes [typical of Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Lazio "Cuisine of Lazio") and [Abruzzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuisine_of_Abruzzo "Cuisine of Abruzzo"), the [regions of Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Italy "Regions of Italy") nearest the Vatican.[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-83)

### General congregations

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: General congregations")\]

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Conclave_Map.svg/250px-Conclave_Map.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Conclave_Map.svg)

Map of the major venues of the conclave

According to Catholic canon law, general congregations are daily meetings of all cardinals regardless of elector status and begin before all of the elector cardinals arrive in Rome. The initial meetings are focused on the logistics of the papal funeral and the conclave, including physical preparations at the Domus Sanctae Marthae (as a dormitory) and the Sistine Chapel (as a polling place). Later ones, typically the eighth and following, shift to discussions about the needs of the church and the world, and the issues facing the Roman Curia.[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-84)[\[84\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-85)[\[85\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-86) These later general congregations are guided by the reflections given by two "distinguished and morally authoritative" clerics who are selected by the cardinals.[\[86\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-87) The cardinals are also given the opportunity to make formal remarks regarding the issues facing the church.[\[87\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-88) All of these speeches and discussions are termed _interventi_ ("interventions") in Italian.[\[88\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-89) The general congregations meet in the New Synod Hall, on the first floor of the vestibule of the much larger [Paul VI Audience Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI_Audience_Hall "Paul VI Audience Hall").[\[89\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-90)[\[90\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-91) For the 2025 conclave, the general congregations met every day from 22 April following Francis's death until 6 May,[\[91\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-92) excluding 26–27 April,[\[92\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-93) 1 May,[\[93\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-94) and 4 May,[\[94\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-95) with the beginning of the conclave proper on 7 May.[\[95\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-96)

General congregations allow the cardinals to meet on their own initiative, thereby getting to know each other and exercise their [spiritual discernment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discernment_in_Christianity "Discernment in Christianity"); many had never met,[\[96\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-97) as Francis did not hold meetings of cardinals before his [papal consistories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_consistory "Papal consistory").[\[97\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-98)[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-120+-15) Furthermore, the cardinals have full access to global media and their diverse analyses and criteria for identifying the _papabile_.[\[98\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-99) Before leaving for Rome on 24 April, Cardinal [Pablo Virgilio David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Virgilio_David "Pablo Virgilio David") stressed that a conclave is not a political campaign but a [religious retreat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retreat_/(spiritual/) "Retreat (spiritual)"). He also emphasized that it is a duty of the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") to discern each other via prayer, [personal letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_letter "Personal letter"), and even research on a website with biographical and other information set up for that purpose,[\[99\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-100) and that it is not a matter of [candidates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candidate "Candidate").[\[100\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-101) Both the formal and informal discussions are expected to be very substantive in preparation for, and in the hope of, a speedy conclave.[\[101\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-102)[\[102\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-103) The discussions held at cardinals' own initiative—_pratiche_, or exercises—are the most frank and candid.[\[103\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-104) By canon law, the congregations are bound to the same secrecy as the conclave.[\[104\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-105)

On 22 April, members of the [papal staff and household](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_staff_and_household "Papal staff and household") were asked to vacate their rooms at the Domus Sanctae Marthae following the death of Pope Francis in his suite on the second floor to allow for conclave preparations in that building to begin.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Il_Mattino-2025-69) The same day, the first of twelve general congregations were held. At the first congregation, the approximately sixty cardinals present listened to [Kevin Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Farrell "Kevin Farrell"), the [Cardinal Camerlengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Camerlengo "Cardinal Camerlengo"), read the [will and testament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament") of Francis. The canonization of [Carlo Acutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlo_Acutis "Carlo Acutis"), originally scheduled to take place in Rome on 27 April, was suspended, and the cardinals confirmed the date for the papal funeral. This meeting also dealt with the logistics of the funeral.[\[105\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-106)[\[106\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-107) The attending cardinals took the oath of secrecy concerning their meetings.[\[107\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-108) Despite the fact that general congregations are closed to non-cardinals, Sister [Simona Brambilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simona_Brambilla "Simona Brambilla"), a [religious sister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_sister "Religious sister") and the first woman to head a Vatican department (the [Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicastery_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life "Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life")), was accidentally sent a standard email inviting her to participate.[\[108\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-109) On 23 April, the [Vatican Museums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Museums "Vatican Museums") announced the closure of the Sistine Chapel beginning on 28 April, due to the needs of the conclave.[\[109\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-110)[\[110\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-111) At the second congregation, the program for the _novendiales_, or nine-day period of mourning for the deceased pope, was approved.[\[111\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-112) Cardinal [Norberto Rivera Carrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norberto_Rivera_Carrera "Norberto Rivera Carrera") stated to the press that these discussions had been mostly procedural in nature, as many cardinals from around the world were still traveling.[\[112\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-113)

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg/250px-Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Assembl%C3%A9e_du_Synode_des_%C3%A9v%C3%AAques_sur_la_famille_en_2014.jpg)

Cardinals and bishops in the [New Synod Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Synod_Hall "New Synod Hall") (pictured in 2014), one of the venues for the general congregations

The third congregation on 24 April, with 113 cardinals present, saw the appointment of the two conclave preachers, [Donato Ogliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donato_Ogliari "Donato Ogliari") and Cardinal [Raniero Cantalamessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raniero_Cantalamessa "Raniero Cantalamessa").[\[113\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-114)[\[114\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-115) At the fourth general congregation on 25 April, the 149 cardinals in attendance listened to a presentation on Francis's funeral rite.[\[115\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-116) By this time nearly 70 formal speeches, or "interventions", had been given.[\[116\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-117) There was also discussion concerning the status of Giovanni Angelo Becciu as a cardinal elector among the participants, which continued in the following congregations until his 29 April acceptance of his non-elector status.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Pinto-2025-22)

The fifth general congregation on 28 April determined that the conclave would begin on 7 May, sixteen days following Francis's death.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5)[\[117\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-118) This meeting also discussed the [clerical sexual abuse crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church_sexual_abuse_cases "Catholic Church sexual abuse cases"), challenges in [evangelization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelization "Evangelization"), and [ecumenism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecumenism "Ecumenism"). Twenty cardinals delivered interventions.[\[118\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-119) Conservative cardinals, such as [Gerhard Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Ludwig_M%C3%BCller "Gerhard Ludwig Müller") and [Francis Arinze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Arinze "Francis Arinze") (not an elector), were particularly vocal during this session.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-White-2025-120)[\[120\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-121) The next day, at the sixth congregation on 29 April, the start time for the conclave was set at 4:30 p.m., and [Cardinal Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Re "Cardinal Re") was chosen as the celebrant for the opening Mass for the conclave.[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122) [Donato Ogliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donato_Ogliari "Donato Ogliari") gave his scheduled reflection to the 183 cardinals present, 124 of them being electors, emphasizing the theme of synodality from the Francis papacy.[\[119\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-White-2025-120)[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122)[\[122\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-123)

The seventh congregation on 30 April featured a discussion of the Vatican's financial issues by the 180 cardinals present, 124 of whom were electors.[\[123\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-124)[\[124\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-125) [Rainer Woelki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainer_Woelki "Rainer Woelki") stated that the meetings thus far had been "fraternal and cordial ... a very concentrated, calm, factual working atmosphere".[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_News_Agency-38) [Beniamino Stella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beniamino_Stella "Beniamino Stella"), not an elector, made a very strongly-worded critique of Francis's decision to allow [lay persons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_laity "Catholic laity") to exercise powers of church governance formerly reserved to [clergy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_orders_in_the_Catholic_Church "Holy orders in the Catholic Church"). This surprised many cardinals, as Stella was viewed as one of Francis's most trusted advisors and a prominent supporter of Parolin.[\[125\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-126)[\[126\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-127)[\[127\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-128)

The general congregation did not meet on 1 May, the feast of [Saint Joseph the Worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_the_Worker "Saint Joseph the Worker"), a [public holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holiday "Public holiday") for the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") and an ecclesiastical counterpart to the secular [International Workers' Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Workers%27_Day "International Workers' Day") observed on the same day.[\[128\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-129) The _[National Catholic Reporter's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Catholic_Reporter "National Catholic Reporter")_ Rome bureau reported that Prevost was "emerging as a serious frontrunner".[\[129\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-130) At the ninth congregation on 2 May, 177 cardinals were present, of whom 127 were electors. Twenty-six cardinals spoke. Among the subjects discussed were: communion (_[koinonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koinonia "Koinonia")_) within the church and fraternity in and with the world; the hope of some that the next pope would be 'prophetic'; and the [2025 Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jubilee "2025 Jubilee").[\[130\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-131) The tenth and eleventh congregations were both held on 5 May and discussed a wide range of church topics.[\[131\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-132)[\[132\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-133) On 6 May, the twelfth and final congregation of the College of Cardinals took place.[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brockhaus-2025-134) This congregation witnessed the ceremonial destruction of Francis' symbols of office: his [fisherman's ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisherman%27s_ring "Fisherman's ring") and [lead seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulla_/(seal/) "Bulla (seal)").[\[133\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brockhaus-2025-134)

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_%2811948661293%29.jpg/250px-A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_%2811948661293%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_Swiss_Guard_Unlocks_the_Door_Outside_of_the_Sistine_Chapel_for_Secretary_Kerry_/(11948661293/).jpg)

The doors of the Sistine Chapel (pictured in 2014) were shut at 5:46 p.m. on 7 May.

On 7 May, the conclave began. It was preceded by Cardinal [Giovanni Battista Re](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovanni_Battista_Re "Giovanni Battista Re"), the dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrating the Mass _pro eligendo Pontifice_ (lit. 'for the election of the Pontiff') in [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica") at 10 am [CEST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Summer_Time "Central European Summer Time") (08:00 UTC).[\[134\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-135) All support staff, such as [sacristans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacristan "Sacristan"), medical staff, elevator operators, and the director of security services for the Vatican, along with officers and officials of the conclave, had taken their solemn oath of secrecy on 5 May.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Catholic_Review-2025-77)[\[135\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-136) At 4:30 pm, the conclave officially began with a prayer service in the [Pauline Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappella_Paolina "Cappella Paolina"), at the end of which the electors entered the Sistine Chapel in procession. Once there, the hymn _[Veni Creator Spiritus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veni_Creator_Spiritus "Veni Creator Spiritus")_ ("Come, Creator Spirit") was sung and the 133 cardinal electors then swore themselves to secrecy.[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-NPR-81)[\[121\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican_News-2025-122)[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brennan-2025-137) Each cardinal elector in order of seniority placed his hands on a [Book of the Gospels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_the_Gospels "Book of the Gospels") and made the affirmation aloud in Latin:[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Povoledo-2025-138)

> > _Et ego_ \[prænomen\] _Cardinalis_ \[nomen\] _spondeo, voveo ac iuro. Sic me Deus adiuvet et haec Sancta Dei Evangelia, quae manu mea tango.[\[138\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-139)_
> 
> Translation:
> 
> > And I, \[forename\] Cardinal \[surname\], do so promise, pledge, and swear. So help me God and these Holy Gospels, which I touch with my hand.[\[137\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Povoledo-2025-138)

While making the oath, several cardinals used the Latin forms of their names.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) [Diego Ravelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Ravelli "Diego Ravelli"), the [papal master of ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_master_of_ceremonies "Papal master of ceremonies"), then called out the words _[Extra omnes](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/extra_omnes "wikt:extra omnes")_, a command for everyone who is not a cardinal elector or an official of the conclave to leave the chamber.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) He then shut the entrance to the Sistine Chapel at 5:46 p.m.[\[136\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Brennan-2025-137)[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) Cardinal [Raniero Cantalamessa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raniero_Cantalamessa "Raniero Cantalamessa"), the longtime Capuchin preacher of the pontifical household, then offered a reflection to the cardinals behind the closed doors.[\[140\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-141) Reportedly, the remarks lasted for over an hour, delaying the start of the first ballot (and, consequently, the smoke reporting out its results); at one point, Cardinal [Parolin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Parolin "Pietro Parolin") asked the assembled cardinal electors if they wanted to postpone the first vote until the next morning — (they did not).[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-:0-142)

Given the conclave had begun in the afternoon, only a single ballot was held on this first day.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zengarini-2025-5) According to some reports, Parolin, the frontrunner, received more than 40 votes on the first ballot, while the rest of the field was considerably split.[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51)[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zurlo-2025-144) According to other reports, [Prevost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIV "Pope Leo XIV") was the most voted candidate in the first ballot, slightly above Parolin, with [Péter Erdő](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P%C3%A9ter_Erd%C5%91 "Péter Erdő"), one of the main conservative candidates, in third place.[\[144\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-145)[\[145\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-146) The first day of the conclave ended at 9:00 p.m., after black smoke emerged from the chimney of the Sistine Chapel, signifying that the vote taken had not resulted in the election of a new pope.[\[139\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Krupa-2025-140) [Vatican Media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Media "Vatican Media") reported that up to 45,000 people had gathered in [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square") to await the smoke.[\[146\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-147)

White smoke billowing from the Sistine Chapel chimney. Faithful onlookers rejoiced, shouting "_[Habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")_!" ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language") for 'We have a pope') and "_Viva il papa_!" ([Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") for 'Long live the pope') in [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square").

[![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg/250px-Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pope_Leo_XIV_on_the_loggia.jpg)

Pope Leo XIV on the loggia of St. Peter's Basilica following his election

The second day of the conclave began with two ballots, concluding at approximately 10:30 a.m. and 11:45 a.m., respectively.[\[147\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-148) Black smoke appeared at 11:51 a.m., again signifying that no pope had been elected. Smoke is not produced after each ballot, but rather only at the end of each session (ballot cards from two unsuccessful votes in a morning session or two votes in an afternoon session are usually burned together once each pair of votes has been completed).[\[148\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-149)[\[149\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-150)[\[150\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-151) According to several reports, during this morning session of day 2, Cardinal Parolin received 40 to 50 votes but failed to pick up support from African and Asian cardinals, some of whom started to support Prevost. Pope Francis's strongest supporters were divided between Cardinals [Jean-Marc Aveline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Marc_Aveline "Jean-Marc Aveline") (France) and [Mario Grech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Grech "Mario Grech") (Malta), while Asian cardinals were splitting their votes between the two Filipino Cardinals [Luis Antonio Tagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Antonio_Tagle "Luis Antonio Tagle") and [Pablo Virgilio David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Virgilio_David "Pablo Virgilio David"). Cardinal Prevost enjoyed broad support from South American and [Anglosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglosphere "Anglosphere") cardinals, thanks also to the strong support of [Timothy Dolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Dolan "Timothy Dolan"), who supposedly functioned as something of a [kingmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingmaker "Kingmaker").[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Agenzia_ANSA-2025-51)[\[143\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Zurlo-2025-144)[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Giusti-2025-152) The cardinals then returned to the Domus Sanctae Marthae for lunch,[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Quotidiano_Nazionale-2025-153) where the breadth of support for Prevost became clearer.[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[\[141\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-:0-142) Cardinals later told the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that the result was becoming clear by the third ballot, as the votes were moving toward Prevost.[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-AP122025-154) Pope Leo XIV later stated that after the third ballot, "I resigned myself to the fact when I saw how things were going and I said 'This could be a reality.'"[\[153\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-AP122025-154) By the end of the morning session, there were 15,000 people in St. Peter's Square and 5,000 people at the basilica of [Santa Maria Maggiore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Santa Maria Maggiore"). More were expected during the afternoon session, since in the two most recent conclaves a new pope had been elected on either the fourth or fifth ballot.[\[154\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-155)

After the lunch recess, the cardinals returned to the Sistine Chapel for the next and fourth round of voting.[\[152\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Quotidiano_Nazionale-2025-153) The cardinals' support coalesced around Prevost, who received more than the two-thirds majority of 89 required: he reportedly received more than 100 votes on the fourth (and final) ballot.[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143)[\[151\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Giusti-2025-152)[\[155\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-156)

Parolin, as the most senior cardinal in the conclave, asked Prevost if he accepted his election as Supreme Pontiff, and by what [papal name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_name "Papal name") he would be known. Having quietly accepted his election, Prevost announced to the cardinals his chosen papal name _Leo_,[\[142\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Meichtry,_Stancati,_Lovett_&_Walker_2025-143) chosen at least in part to honor [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII").[\[156\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-157)[\[157\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-158) Following the pope's acceptance of his election, the cardinals applauded, and he embraced them. He then exited the Sistine Chapel to the Room of Tears to be robed in the garments prepared there for the new pope.

After the fourth round of voting, white smoke appeared at 6:07 p.m., followed by the ringing of the bells of St. Peter's Basilica, confirming and signifying the election of a new pope.[\[158\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-159)[\[159\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-160)[\[160\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-161) Soon afterwards, the [Swiss Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Guard "Swiss Guard") and members of the [Italian Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Armed_Forces "Italian Armed Forces"), along with the bands of the [Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gendarmerie_Corps_of_Vatican_City_State "Gendarmerie Corps of Vatican City State") and the [Carabinieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carabinieri "Carabinieri"), paraded through St. Peter's Square and took up formation beneath the central [loggia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loggia "Loggia") of St. Peter's Basilica. From there, Cardinal Protodeacon [Dominique Mamberti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Mamberti "Dominique Mamberti") announced the election of Prevost[\[161\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Wooden-2025-162) and that he had taken the papal name _Leo XIV_.[\[162\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Associated_Press-2025-163)[\[163\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-164)

| --- |
| [![Image 7: video icon](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) [Announcement](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E57t_CUjBmk) of the election of Robert Francis Prevost as Pope Leo XIV |

Leo XIV stepped onto the balcony shortly after the official announcement of his election, spoke to the crowd in St. Peter's Square and the world in Italian (while also briefly speaking in [Peruvian Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peruvian_Spanish "Peruvian Spanish") to acknowledge the [Diocese of Chiclayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Chiclayo "Roman Catholic Diocese of Chiclayo"), where he previously served as Bishop), expressed gratitude for Francis's legacy,[\[164\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-165) then delivered the _[Urbi et Orbi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbi_et_Orbi "Urbi et Orbi")_ blessing.[\[161\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Wooden-2025-162) He was accompanied by Ravelli, Marco Agostini, and Jean-Jacques Didier Bouable, who led the group as [cross-bearer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucifer "Crucifer"). The three were from the [Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_for_the_Liturgical_Celebrations_of_the_Supreme_Pontiff "Office for the Liturgical Celebrations of the Supreme Pontiff").\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Immediately after the appearance of white smoke, 40,000 were present in St. Peter's Square;[\[165\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-166) according to Italian law enforcement, by the time of the _[habemus papam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habemus_papam "Habemus papam")_ announcement, there were up to 150,000 in the square.[\[166\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-167)

Post-conclave events
--------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2025_conclave&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Post-conclave events")\]

The Holy See Press Office announced the schedule of activities and liturgical celebrations following the election of Pope Leo XIV.[\[167\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-168) He celebrated his first Mass as pope with the [College of Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_Cardinals "College of Cardinals") in the Sistine Chapel at 11:00 am on 9 May 2025, the day after his election.[\[168\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-169) On 10 May 2025, he met the College of Cardinals in the Synod Hall.[\[169\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-170) In the morning of 11 May, he celebrated a private Mass at the [Vatican Grottoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Grottoes "Vatican Grottoes"),[\[170\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-171) paying homage to his predecessors, before delivering his first _[Regina caeli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regina_caeli "Regina caeli")_ address from the central loggia of [St. Peter's Basilica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica "St. Peter's Basilica").[\[171\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-172) After the address, Leo broke the seals to the [papal apartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_apartments "Papal apartments") of the [Apostolic Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace "Apostolic Palace"), accompanied by Parolin and Farrell.[\[172\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-173)

Pope Leo XIV celebrated his [inauguration Mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_inauguration_of_Pope_Leo_XIV "Papal inauguration of Pope Leo XIV") on 18 May 2025 at [St. Peter's Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square "St. Peter's Square").[\[173\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-174)[\[174\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-Vatican-Inauguration-2025-175) He took canonical possession of the three other major basilicas on 20 May ([Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Paul_Outside_the_Walls "Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls")) and 25 May ([Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbasilica_of_Saint_John_Lateran "Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran") and [Basilica of St. Mary Major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Maria_Maggiore "Santa Maria Maggiore")).[\[175\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-176) He had his first general audience on 21 May. On 24 May, he met the Roman Curia and the Vatican City State employees. On 31 May, he conferred his first presbyteral ordination as bishop of Rome to the priests of the [Diocese of Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Rome "Diocese of Rome").[\[176\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_conclave#cite_note-177)

Pope Leo XIV tries a new digital platform of the Vatican's yearbook, known as the Annuario Pontificio, at the Vatican Dec. 6, 2025. (CNS photo/screengrab courtesy Vatican Secretary of State)

Vatican yearbook goes online
============================

![Image 3](https://catholicreview.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/CNS-logo-240-opt-1-100x100.jpg) December 10, 2025  
By [Carol Glatz](https://catholicreview.org/author/carol-glatz/)  
Catholic News Service Filed Under: [Feature](https://catholicreview.org/category/feature/), [News](https://catholicreview.org/category/news/), [Vatican](https://catholicreview.org/category/vatican/)

VATICAN CITY (CNS) — The Vatican’s fat red yearbook, known as the Annuario Pontificio, will now be available and updated regularly on an app and online.

The digital platform “will guarantee reliable and immediate access to certified content, promoting an accurate and documented account of the life of the church,” the Vatican Secretariat of State said in a press release Dec. 9.

The pontifical yearbook lists: all Vatican offices and staff; the world’s dioceses and mission territories; bishops, cardinals and international religious orders of men and women; papal diplomats and ambassadors to the Vatican; historical notes, such as a list of the popes and their years in office, and more.

Archbishop Edgar Peña Parra, substitute for general affairs in the secretariat, and others met with Pope Leo XIV Dec. 6 to present the initiative and to let him try searching the platform on a tablet.

“Thank you for this work, which will be of great use to so many people who work serving the church,” the pope told those present. “I encourage you to continue in this spirit of service, so that what is established with care and attention may become an even greater help over time.”

Archbishop Parra said, “The digitization of the Pontifical Yearbook represents a significant step in the renewal of the Holy See’s tools of service. At a time when communication is increasingly rapid and global, offering immediate and reliable access to information on the life of the church — with certified data — means putting technology at the service of the church’s mission.”

The thick, hardcover yearbook typically numbers more than 2,500 pages and is available only in Italian. Printed once a year, the Vatican used to send out changes and updates once or twice a month via email and post them online. Officials from the Secretariat of State are responsible for updating the volume.

Now, as a digital resource, information will be revised and updated more often, the secretariat’s press release said.

After creating an account online and paying the annual subscription fee ($79), the online version is available at annuariopontificio.catholic or on an app optimized for smartphones and tablets.

After the initial rollout, the platform will add expanded capabilities, such as other languages and past data for archival purposes.

The hardcopy volume will still be published, the secretariat said, because of the historical value of such documentation.
